title: Quantization execution path specs - INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ (draft v3)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures constraints, kernel expectations, scheduling implications, and KV-cache interactions for supporting INT8, FP8, GPTQ, and AWQ quantized models in the serving runtime. It’s a working spec for eng-serving-runtime to drive kernel contracts, execution-path variants, and rollout constraints for Dedicated/Hosted/Private.

Scope:
- Supported quant formats: per-tensor/per-channel INT8, FP8 (E4M3/E5M2), GPTQ (per-row scaling), AWQ (asymmetric weight quant)
- Focus on transformer decoder-only and encoder-decoder for inference (sampling, streaming, and chat workloads)
- Covers kernel constraints, memory layout, dequant strategies, KV cache compatibility, batching and scheduling, fallback policies

Background / motivation:
We need explicit execution-paths that allow the scheduler to reason about latency/cost tradeoffs and fallbacks when certain kernels/hardware are unavailable. Quantized models reduce memory/BW and enable higher throughput, but introduce constraints (alignment, mixed-precision intermediate compute, reduced numeric range) that affect KV cache handling and streaming latency.

High-level execution path overview:
- Profile-driven selection: runtime selects path based on model metadata (quant format per-layer), hardware capabilities (tensor cores, int8 fma, fp8 support), and availability of optimized kernels in the current binary.
- Paths:
  1) Native-quant fused kernels: attention/ffn kernels that operate on quantized weights without full dequant to FP32 per call.
  2) Block-dequant kernels: dequantize weight-blocks to FP16/TF32 in L2/L3 cache, perform compute in FP16, re-use dequantized block across micro-batches.
  3) Full dequant fallback: dequantize all weights to FP16/FP32 on load (largest memory + latency), used when optimized kernels missing.

Kernel constraints (per quant type):
- INT8 (symmetric/per-channel):
  - Kernel must accept packed int8 weights + scale and zero-point vectors (per-channel optional).
  - Activation compute can be FP16/TF32. Kernel may implement requantize for outputs when stacking quantized layers.
  - Alignment: weight columns must be padded to 32 or 64 for vectorized matmul depending on target ISA.
  - KV cache: attention keys/values remain FP16/FP32. If attention projection weights are int8, projection kernels must dequantize outputs to FP16 to generate keys/values.

- FP8 (E4M3/E5M2):
  - Kernel must handle exponent/scale metadata; prefer FP16 intermediate accumulation to prevent overflow.
  - Hardware: prefer tensor cores or instruction sets with FP8 support; otherwise block-dequant to FP16.
  - Numerical safeguards: apply per-layer bias-correction factors derived from calibration pass when using fused FP8->FP16 compute.
  - KV cache: store cached K/V in FP16/FP32. If model uses FP8 activations, we decode activations to FP16 before caching.

- GPTQ (per-row scaling + rMSE correction):
  - Kernel must accept compressed weight representation (quantized weights + scales + optional permutation/prefix data) and apply per-row dequant on-the-fly to FP16 accumulators.
  - Prefetch: kernels should support streaming dequant for weight tiles to hide memory latency.
  - Determinism: GPTQ introduces small numeric differences; runtime must record model-variant id to ensure deterministic run configuration for experiment comparisons.
  - KV cache: same as INT8 - projected outputs are FP16.

- AWQ (asymmetric weight quant):
  - Kernel must accept int8 + zero-point + multiplier arrays; dequant performed to FP16 in-register when possible.
  - Storage layout: store quant params contiguous with weights to optimize load/store.
  - KV cache: projection outputs must be computed into FP16 for caching.

Memory layout and loading rules:
- Quantized weights stored in packed format on disk/OCI layers with accompanying metadata file (.quant.meta) enumerating per-layer quant type, scales, zero-points, row/col granularity, and pinning hints.
- Runtime must validate the metadata before binding kernels; mismatch triggers graceful fallback.
- Dequant buffer pool: maintain a small LRU pool of dequantized tiles (FP16) per model to support block-dequant path. Size configurable via model config (default: 128MB).

KV cache interactions:
- KV cache remains FP16/FP32 regardless of weight quantization. Decision rationale: reduces accumulated rounding error over long contexts and simplifies cross-variant compatibility.
- When attention projection uses quantized weights, the projection kernel must output FP16 keys/values. Kernel contract: signature includes output dtype and quantization metadata.
- Cache invalidation: switching execution path mid-session (e.g., due to fallback) requires flush/recompute of cached K/V for any live session to avoid mixed numeric paths.

Scheduling, batching, and latency considerations:
- Micro-batching: fused quant kernels enable larger micro-batch sizes with lower per-token cost, but may increase tail latency for single-token streaming requests. Scheduler should prefer block-dequant for low-latency single-streams and fused kernels for high-throughput batched workloads.
- Priority routing: per-request routing flags allow forcing "low-latency" or "high-throughput" execution path.
- Cost model: add per-path cost estimates into request cost calculation (tokens/sec, memory, expected p99). These are populated from offline benchmarks per hardware family.
- Pre-warming: for models using block-dequant, pre-warm dequant pool on model load if the model is tagged sustained-heavy.

Fallbacks and compatibility matrix:
- If a hardware-optimized fused kernel is missing, runtime attempts block-dequant path. If dequant pool insufficient or memory constrained, falls back to full dequant (FP16) or rejects request with model-unavailable when memory limit prevents safe fallback.
- Model metadata flags unsupported features (e.g., FP8 E5M2) and runtime advertises which features are available in binary.
- Rollout policy: canary small percentage of traffic to new fused-kernel path; automatic rollback on perf/regression alarms.

Testing and benchmarks:
- Required benchmarks per quant path:
  - single-stream p50/p95/p99 latency for sampling (temperature=0.8, top_p=0.95)
  - batched throughput (batch sizes 1/4/8/32) with and without KV cache reuse
  - memory footprint (resident set size) and GPU memory utilisation
  - numerical validation against FP32 baseline using evaluation prompt set, report perplexity and generation diffs
- Regression tolerances: maximum acceptable delta vs FP32: perplexity +1.5% (hard), human eval metric drop <=2% for LLM tasks (TBD per model family)

Rollout plan and ops:
- Deliverable kernel contract docs and C API by end of sprint.
- Implement feature flag that selects quant execution path per model instance.
- Monitoring: add quant-path tag to traces and dashboards; track errors, fallback rates, latency deltas, and rerun evals on code deploy.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we store KV cache in FP16 only or provide hybrid FP16/FP32 option for extreme-context customers? (action: SRE + Sizing)
- Quantized attention fusion across multi-heads - can we support fused multi-head projection without explicit dequant per head? (action: APPLIED-ML)
- Formalize numeric correction factors for FP8 per-layer calibration; need tools to compute and bake into .quant.meta (action: research)
- Provide guidance for toolchain to produce .quant.meta (converter + tests) - interface here needs spec.

Action items:
- Ava: draft C API prototypes (kernel signature, metadata bindings) - due 2025-03-07
- Jonah: run microbench baseline on A100/3090/RTX-class for INT8 and FP8 fused vs block-dequant - due 2025-03-14
- Lina: spec .quant.meta schema and validator tool - due 2025-03-10
- Marcus: integrate quant-path tag into tracing and add dashboard widgets - due 2025-03-21

References / linked artifacts:
- CONFLUENCE: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/quantization-exec-paths
- GH PR (kernel prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4567
- Jira: SERV-789, QUANT-102, MLPERF-111

Notes (informal):
- This is still a draft. Expect many small changes to kernel ABI after first prototype. Keep backward-compatible metadata versioning in mind.
- Prefer de-risked partial rollout: start with INT8 (most mature) -> GPTQ/AWQ -> FP8 once HW-specific kernels land.
